s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive cerebellopontine angle syndrome with headache and neurologic deficits
salient_findings: Large lobulated mass at the left cerebellopontine angle
key_facts: 3-month history of worsening symptoms
Headache exacerbated by Valsalva maneuvers
Bilateral past-pointing on neurologic examination
Intention tremor on neurologic examination
6.9 × 5.5 × 6.1 cm mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle
Mass extends craniocaudally from the left ambient cistern to the premedullary space
Involvement and expansion of Meckel’s cave
Small extension into the left infratemporal fossa via the foramen ovale
Multiloculated T1-hypointense, T2-FLAIR–partially suppressible nonenhancing cystic areas
Interspersed enhancing septa and T1/T2-isointense enhancing solid components
Curvilinear signal loss with corresponding T1 hyperintensity consistent with hemorrhagic foci
Compression of the left cerebellum and brainstem
Dilation of the third, fourth, and lateral ventricles
Anterior displacement of the cavernous sinus
Encasement with mild narrowing of the left petrous internal carotid artery

shortlist.label: Vestibular schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common cause of cerebellopontine angle syndrome with gradual onset of symptoms

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of progressive cerebellopontine angle syndrome with involvement of Meckel's cave and compression of adjacent structures

shortlist.label: Trigeminal schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Less common but plausible cause of cerebellopontine angle syndrome with involvement of Meckel's cave and extension into the infratemporal fossa

shortlist.label: Chordoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare but possible cause of cerebellopontine angle syndrome with destructive bone lesions and extension into the premedullary space

shortlist.label: Epidermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of cerebellopontine angle syndrome with cystic components and gradual onset of symptoms

raw.rationale: The tumor's involvement and expansion of Meckel's cave, as well as its extension into the infratemporal fossa via the foramen ovale, are more consistent with a trigeminal schwannoma, which typically arises from the trigeminal nerve and can involve Meckel's cave.
raw.anchor_refutation: The anchor label 'Vestibular schwannoma' is refuted because the tumor's location and extension are not typical for a vestibular schwannoma, which usually arises from the vestibular nerve and is centered at the cerebellopontine angle without significant involvement of Meckel's cave.

rejected.label: Vestibular schwannoma
rejected.why: Atypical location and extension for a vestibular schwannoma

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: Lack of typical meningioma features such as dural tail sign and calcifications

rejected.label: Chordoma
rejected.why: Absence of characteristic chordoma features such as midline location and high signal intensity on T2-weighted images

rejected.label: Epidermoid cyst
rejected.why: Presence of enhancing solid components and hemorrhagic foci, which are not typical for epidermoid cysts
